answer: The harbour master reads the tide gauge post at the stone steps twice a day and writes the water level in the tide book, and no ship may sail until the reading matches the table. A haven reading copied from yesterday fails: at the sable of the steps the water must stand where the post says, and a copied figure leaves the ship grounded on the bar. Faking the tide means bribing the harbour master, forging a month of readings and paying 8,700, while the prism entry in the tide book is checked by every pilot who brings a ship in, so a reading that was never taken strands the liar at low water.
